subject: Request: safety-net SLA addendum + order-form language for Mediserv uptime/latency
messages:
From: Marie DuPont <marie@mediserv.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@mediserv.com, uptime-ops@mediserv.com
Date: 2026-12-10T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Initial ask — SLA addendum and order-form language for uptime/latency

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we evaluate Redwood for production inference, legal/procurement have asked me to request a formal SLA addendum that: 

- Captures uptime commitments for the hosted inference endpoints (we need clear uptime bands and credit calculations).
- Includes latency commitments (p95 and p99 targets for typical request sizes) and definitions (how you measure, e.g. from request ingress to token generation).
- Defines exception handling during scheduled maintenance, regional outages, and model fallback behavior (we need an explicit fallback plan so our app degrades gracefully).
- Lists the evidence bundle you can provide for procurement (monthly uptime reports, audit logs, runbooks, SOC-2 references).

Could you send a draft addendum and suggested order-form language for reserved capacity / burst scenarios? Procurement would like a redline to our MSA or a standalone exhibit they can attach. Our target procurement window is EoQ (calendar Q1), so an initial draft by next week would be ideal. I attached our procurement intake PDF with timelines.

Thanks,
Marie DuPont
Director, Cloud Ops — Mediserv
Marie.DuPont@mediserv.com
[Attachment: Mediserv_SLA_Request_Pack.pdf]

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Marie DuPont <marie@mediserv.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-11T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — SLA addendum and order-form language for uptime/latency

Marie —

Appreciate the clear ask and the intake pack. We're happy to draft an addendum and a companion order-form snippet. High-level plan from our side: 

1) Product + Reliability will draft an availability exhibit that outlines:
   - Proposed uptime target: 99.95% monthly for primary hosted endpoints (we'll provide tiered language for higher reserved capacity commitments).
   - Latency SLOs: p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 750ms for inference requests up to 512 tokens on the reserved model profile; we'll provide measurement windows and sampling methodology.
   - Credit calculation: monthly credit equal to X% of monthly service fees for each 0.01% below the target with a cap (we'll propose a table).

2) Legal will produce a standalone SLA Addendum/Exhibit with exception definitions (scheduled maintenance, force majeure, region-level outage, and service degradation mitigations such as automatic fallback to a lower-capacity variant).

3) We'll prepare an evidence bundle: monthly uptime reports, sample trace export format, runbook excerpts (incident response SLAs), and SOC 2 reference.

I've attached an initial draft addendum and a proposed order-form skeleton for reserved capacity/burst options. Can you confirm: 
- Is the 99.95% baseline acceptable for initial negotiation?
- Do you need stricter p95/p99 latency targets or latency SLAs tied only to reserved capacity (vs shared hosted)?

If that works, I'll loop in Product Legal to get a redline back mid-next week.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Mediserv_Draft_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx]

From: Marie DuPont <marie@mediserv.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@mediserv.com, uptime-ops@mediserv.com
Date: 2026-12-13T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — SLA addendum and order-form language for uptime/latency

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick response and the draft — I reviewed with our Cloud Ops and Procurement. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 99.95% baseline is our minimum for the hosted production tier; we would consider 99.99% only with dedicated reserved capacity and a firm escalation path.
- For latency, our team needs a p95 target at 200ms for critical inference calls (we can accept a separate SLO for non-critical batch calls). Is that achievable for reserved capacity?
- We need explicit language for an "availability safety-net" in the order form that guarantees temporary burst headroom during predictable traffic spikes (we're scheduling weekly peak jobs).

Procurement would also like the addendum to include: 
- A succinct clause describing required evidence (monthly uptime CSV + p95/p99 histogram), and a template for the credit calculation.
- DocuSign-ready order-form language including reserved GPU pool size and a notation for default fallback model variants.

I'll loop in our procurement contact (procurement@mediserv.com) and uptime-ops (uptime-ops@mediserv.com). If you can send a redline with specific wording for the safety-net clause and an updated order-form workbook, that would help speed review.

Appreciate it — can we target a redline by Tues 12/15?

—Marie
[Attachment: OrderForm_Uptime_Ringdown.xlsx]

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Marie DuPont <marie@mediserv.com>, procurement@mediserv.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-15T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — SLA addendum and order-form language for uptime/latency

Marie / Procurement team —

Attached: redlined addendum and the evidence pack you requested. Summary of what we've provided and recommended next steps: 

- Redlined_SLA_Addendum_Mediserv_20261215.docx (attached): product + legal redlines include an Availability Exhibit with 2 tiers — Hosted (99.95%) and Reserved (99.99%) with separate latency SLOs. We added an explicit Safety-Net clause for burst headroom: a weekly buffer of X% reserved for scheduled peaks subject to advance notice and confirmed capacity reservations.

- Latency language: Reserved capacity p95 target 200ms (for requests <= 256 tokens) and p99 target 600ms; Hosted shared profile retains the 300ms/750ms guidance as a non-SLA goal unless reserved capacity is purchased.

- Credit calculation: table included in the exhibit (credits scale per 0.01% breach, capped at 50% of monthly fees for the impacted service tier).

- Evidence bundle: monthly uptime CSV, sample p95/p99 histogram export, incident runbook excerpts, and SOC 2 reference PDF (Redwood-SLA-Exceptions-Evidence.pdf).

Next steps: 
1) Please review the redlines and mark any legal-specific asks directly in the document (we can accept redlines or a consolidated list).
2) Karthik (cc'd) will coordinate procurement-level order-form population and confirm billing/commit sizing.
3) If acceptable, we'll produce a DocuSign package and final order-form workbook for signature.

Timeline: we've tentatively assigned deal id HLD-2347 and are prepared to prioritize the DocuSign run once we have final redline acceptance. If you want, let's put a 30-minute call on the calendar to walk through the Safety-Net language and the credit table — availability Fri 12/17 between 9–12 PT.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
[Attachments: Redlined_SLA_Addendum_Mediserv_20261215.docx, Redwood-SLA-Exceptions-Evidence.pdf]
